extracted.intended_audience: ACUS staff, consultants, committee members, Assembly and Council members, and stakeholders interested in how ACUS recommendations and statements are developed
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for producing ACUS Recommendations or Statements: commissioning studies, preparing comprehensive research reports, committee drafting, Council/Assembly approval, and implementation. Also explains when a Statement (vs. Recommendation) is used and how it is recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory purpose of ACUS recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should serve ACUS's statutory role of convening public and private sector perspectives and proposing improvements to administrative/regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation and engagement of study
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies that lead to recommendations must be formally initiated by the Office of the Chairman and require Council approval to engage consultants; in-house staff may perform the study instead of consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product of the study should be a comprehensive research report that sets forth proposed recommendations—i.e., research must substantiate and motivate the recommendations presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee review and draft Recommendation preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee must review the research report, draft a Recommendation based on the report, and follow the internal approval channel: submit the draft to the Council for approval before forwarding to the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council and Assembly approval sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee submits a draft Recommendation to the Council and, with the Council's approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council approval is a required gate prior to presenting a draft Recommendation to the Assembly for consideration and adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly debate and adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption of a Recommendation occurs after Assembly debate; the Assembly's adoption is the final organizational act that formalizes the Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation obligation for adopted Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS undertakes to implement [the adopted] final Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the Assembly adopts a Recommendation, ACUS commits to undertaking implementation efforts associated with that Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and nature of 'Statements' instead of Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject. ACUS statements are typically the product of the same process that leads to recommendations, but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the goal is to express views, outline issues or conclusions, or provide comments rather than make formal prescriptive recommendations, ACUS may adopt a Statement produced via the same committee/report/approval process; Statements are included alongside Recommendations in ACUS's searchable database.
